core_obligations: Exactness (proof lines 4670-4684): the exactness of f^{-1} on sheaves of sets, and hence on abelian sheaves, is deduced from the description of f^{-1} by colimits, which shows that it commutes with finite limits and colimits.

Stalks (proof lines 4687-4708): part (3) is a general fact about stalks of pullbacks, identified for the small etale site by writing the stalk at a geometric point as a colimit over etale neighbourhoods of the point.
Representable sheaves (proof lines 4711-4723): part (4) is proved either by identifying the colimits defining f^{-1}h_V, or by using the previous parts; the author gives both routes.
proof_roadmap: Get exactness from the colimit description of the inverse image.
Identify stalks of pullbacks through the colimit description of stalks.
Identify f^{-1}h_V with the representable sheaf of the fibre product, either directly or through the other parts.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four properties of the small inverse image: exactness on abelian sheaves and on sheaves of sets, the identification of stalks under pullback, and the identity f^{-1}h_V = h_{X x_Y V} (statement lines 4648-4668). Each part is proved separately inside the counted span: exactness from the colimit description of the inverse image (proof lines 4670-4684), the stalk computation through the description of stalks as colimits over etale neighbourhoods (proof lines 4687-4708), and the representable case, for which the author offers two arguments, one direct and one through the previous parts (proof lines 4711-4723). The content is the comparison of colimits in each case. The claim is H2: four short computations of the same flavour.
